takeaway: Pain on passive stretch of the big toe points to flexor hallucis longus, which lies in the deep posterior compartment of the leg.

question.text: Hours after tibial nailing, a man has excruciating pain on passive extension of the big toe; no neurovascular deficit. What is the likely diagnosis?

answer.text: Compartment syndrome of the deep posterior compartment of the leg

lines.text: A tibial nail, three hours ago, and now terrible pain.
In compartment syndrome, pain is worsened by passive stretching of the affected muscles.
Here the big toe is stretched, and it screams. That stretches flexor hallucis longus.
The ankle movements hurt much less, so the problem is not the calf bulk.
Flexor hallucis longus sits in the deep posterior compartment, with flexor digitorum longus and tibialis posterior.
The anterior compartment holds the extensors instead. So the answer is the deep posterior compartment.
lines.say: (sigh) The anterior compartment holds the extensors instead. So the answer is the deep posterior compartment.
